radiology_report:
UMCG Radiology | 10 February 2025 | Multiparametric Prostate MRI
Clinical Indication:
Re-evaluation for suspected prostate carcinoma in a 71-year-old male with a rising PSA value of 13.0 and a previously positive biopsy.
FINDINGS:
The gland measures 72.0 mL overall. T2-weighted sequences highlight a sharply demarcated, focally hypointense focus measuring approximately 18 mm within the right peripheral zone at the base-to-mid transition. Diffusion-weighted imaging shows pronounced restriction alongside corresponding low signal on the ADC map, aligning with high cellular density. Dynamic contrast-enhanced sequences exhibit early, focal enhancement compared to adjacent tissue. There is no evidence of extracapsular extension or seminal vesicle invasion. Neurovascular bundles remain intact. Pelvic imaging reveals no suspicious lymphadenopathy.
IMPRESSION:
PI-RADS 5 lesion in the right peripheral zone (base/mid), highly suspicious for clinically significant prostate cancer.
Prostate volume: 72.0 mL.
PSA density: 0.18 ng/mL/mL.
csPCa predicted probability 0.78197306.

previous_notes.author: Dr. H. Martens (GP)
previous_notes.text: Clinical review took place in October 2024 after the earlier positive biopsy results returned. Laboratory testing showed a PSA value of 11.1 ng/mL, reflecting a minor decrease from the January high yet still considerably elevated. Mild lower urinary tract symptoms persist, currently controlled with tamsulosin and yielding an IPSS score of 2/35. The ongoing PSA elevation alongside previously documented ISUP GG 3 pathology prompted an outpatient urology referral for comprehensive assessment.
